scenario_text: A mid-sized private bank currently runs its core banking system on a legacy COBOL framework. Management has decided to migrate the entire system to a modern Java-based framework. No new functionality is to be added — the migrated system must replicate the existing features exactly. Testing and validation is required at every stage of the migration to ensure nothing breaks. The project team consists of 2 developers and needs to be completed within 3-4 months.

requirements.statement: The system shall replicate all existing functional features of the legacy COBOL core banking system in the new Java-based framework without adding new functionality.
requirements.business_justification: To ensure business continuity and maintain operational parity during migration, preventing any disruption to daily banking operations or loss of existing capabilities.
requirements.assumptions: A complete inventory of legacy features and data structures is available for analysis before migration begins.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Functional testing confirms that every transaction type, report, and user interface element from the legacy system produces identical results in the new system.

requirements.statement: The system shall execute automated regression tests at every stage of the migration process to verify that no existing functionality is broken.
requirements.business_justification: To detect and prevent data corruption, logic errors, or feature regressions immediately after code translation or module integration.
requirements.assumptions: A comprehensive test suite covering all legacy business rules exists or can be derived from the legacy system's behavior.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Test execution logs show 100% pass rate for regression suites at each migration milestone with zero critical defects.

requirements.statement: The system shall maintain data integrity and consistency throughout the migration process to ensure no data loss or corruption occurs.
requirements.business_justification: Financial institutions cannot tolerate data loss; accurate migration is critical for regulatory compliance and customer trust.
requirements.assumptions: The legacy COBOL system allows read-only access to source data during the migration window.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Post-migration reconciliation reports confirm that record counts, checksums, and field-level values match exactly between legacy and new systems.
applicable_regulations: Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §14 (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023]

requirements.statement: The system shall support a phased or parallel migration strategy to minimize downtime during the transition from COBOL to Java.
requirements.business_justification: To allow for safe cutover and rollback if issues arise, ensuring minimal impact on customer transactions.
requirements.assumptions: The legacy system supports read-only access or can be run in parallel with the new system during cutover.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System availability remains above 99.9% during migration windows, and rollback procedures are successfully tested.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide detailed audit logs for all data transformations and migration activities to support forensic analysis and compliance.
requirements.business_justification: Regulatory bodies require traceability of data movements during major system changes to ensure accountability and detect unauthorized modifications.
requirements.assumptions: The Java framework supports logging infrastructure that can capture migration-specific events.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Audit logs record every data row migrated, transformation rule applied, and error encountered with timestamps and user IDs.

requirements.statement: The system shall display a real-time status indicator on the user interface showing whether the legacy COBOL service or the new Java service is currently active for each transaction type.
requirements.business_justification: With only 2 developers and a tight 3-4 month schedule, the team cannot manually verify every switch-over; users need immediate visual feedback to know if they are interacting with the old system (during failover) or the new one.

requirements.statement: The system shall automatically retry failed data synchronization jobs between the legacy and new systems up to three times before escalating the error to an operations dashboard.
requirements.business_justification: Network timeouts or temporary database locks are common during migration; automatic retries prevent unnecessary manual intervention for transient failures while ensuring eventual consistency.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow administrators to configure specific thresholds for data volume and transaction speed that trigger an alert when the new Java framework performance deviates from the legacy baseline.
requirements.business_justification: Since the goal is exact replication, the system must detect performance regressions immediately so the team can adjust resources or rollback before customer impact exceeds acceptable limits.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a 'dry-run' mode that simulates data migration and transformation logic without actually writing to the production database, allowing validation of complex COBOL business rules.
requirements.business_justification: Given the constraint of 'no new functionality,' the team must rigorously validate that the Java code interprets legacy COBOL logic correctly before committing any data changes.

requirements.statement: The system shall generate a daily reconciliation report comparing transaction counts and balances between the legacy COBOL system and the new Java system for all accounts processed in the previous 24 hours.
requirements.business_justification: Continuous validation is required at every stage; automated daily reports provide the necessary evidence to stakeholders that data integrity (REQ-003) is being maintained throughout the phased migration.

requirements.statement: The system shall archive all raw transaction logs and transformation records from the legacy COBOL system in a read-only format immediately after successful processing to preserve historical data for forensic analysis.
requirements.business_justification: Even if functionality is replicated exactly, the underlying storage technology changes; archiving ensures that original COBOL data remains accessible for audit trails without cluttering the new Java database.

requirements.statement: The system shall enforce a role-based access control (RBAC) model where only developers and designated migration leads can trigger rollback procedures or modify migration configuration parameters.
requirements.business_justification: With a small team of 2 developers working under high pressure, strict segregation of duties is essential to prevent accidental data corruption during the critical migration window.

issues.description: The stakeholder field is empty ('Not specified'). Requirements must identify the source of the requirement.
issues.suggestion: Identify and record the specific stakeholder (e.g., 'Product Owner' or 'UX Lead') responsible for this UI requirement.

issues.description: The term 'real-time' is vague without a defined latency threshold.
issues.suggestion: Define 'real-time' with a specific metric, e.g., 'status updates shall appear within 200ms of the backend state change.'.

issues.description: The requirement assumes the system can distinguish between 'legacy COBOL service' and 'new Java service' active states for 'each transaction type' during a migration where features are being replicated. If REQ-001 is met (identical results), the services are functionally identical, making the distinction of 'which one is active' potentially logically inconsistent unless referring to infrastructure routing which is not defined.
issues.suggestion: Clarify if this refers to a specific routing flag or if the UI should simply indicate 'System Under Maintenance' vs 'Normal Operation'. The current phrasing implies a capability that contradicts the goal of functional parity.

issues.description: The stakeholder field is empty ('Not specified').
issues.suggestion: Identify the specific stakeholder (e.g., 'DevOps Lead' or 'Data Engineer').

issues.description: The term 'escalate' is vague regarding the action taken.
issues.suggestion: Define what 'escalating the error to an operations dashboard' entails (e.g., 'create a high-priority ticket', 'send a webhook notification', or 'change status to ERROR').

issues.description: The stakeholder field is empty ('Not specified').
issues.suggestion: Identify the specific stakeholder (e.g., 'Performance Engineer' or 'SRE').

issues.description: The term 'performance deviates from the legacy baseline' is unmeasurable without defining how the baseline is calculated or stored.
issues.suggestion: Specify if the baseline is a static value, a moving average, or a specific percentage threshold (e.g., 'response time > 1.2x legacy baseline').

issues.description: The term 'dry-run' mode is used without a concrete definition of what constitutes a successful simulation versus a failure, making the acceptance criteria vague.
issues.suggestion: Define specific exit codes or log markers that indicate a successful dry-run simulation versus an error state.
Identify and record the specific stakeholder or business unit requesting this feature.

issues.description: The term 'daily' is vague regarding the exact execution time window (e.g., 00:00 UTC, end of business day) and the definition of 'previous 24 hours' for batch processing.
issues.suggestion: Specify the exact timestamp or cron schedule (e.g., 'at 01:00 UTC daily') and define the precise start/end boundaries for the 'previous 24 hours' calculation.
Identify and record the specific stakeholder or business unit requesting this feature.

issues.description: The term 'immediately' is not measurable; it does not specify a latency threshold (e.g., within 5 minutes, within 1 hour).
issues.suggestion: Replace 'immediately' with a specific time-bound metric (e.g., 'within 5 minutes of successful processing').
Identify and record the specific stakeholder or business unit requesting this feature.

sdlc.summary: Spiral is recommended over Waterfall because it explicitly handles unstable funding (PTR-4) and non-enhancement projects (PTR-3), whereas Waterfall assumes stable funding and system integration. The tie-breaker would be PTR-4: if the project had stable long-term funding, Waterfall might become a stronger candidate.
sdlc.shortcut: High risk legacy replication + unstable short-term funding + long-lived product -> Spiral
sdlc.cross_check_reasoning: The V-Shaped model is the most suitable because it explicitly pairs each development phase with a corresponding verification and validation stage, which is critical for high-risk data migration and regulatory compliance requirements. This structured approach ensures that automated regression tests and data integrity checks are rigorously planned and executed alongside the functional replication of legacy features.

controls.title: Integrations authenticated, encrypted and rate-limited
controls.proposed_requirement: Every integration with an external system shall be mutually authenticated, encrypted in transit, allow-listed and rate-limited, with failures logged.

controls.title: Sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit
controls.proposed_requirement: The system shall encrypt customer and transaction data at rest and in transit using algorithms and key lengths approved under the bank's cryptographic policy.

risk_register.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery for the system
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §28 (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall have a disaster recovery arrangement with defined recovery time and recovery point objectives, tested periodically under the bank's business continuity plan.

risk_register.title: Cyber incidents reported to CERT-In within 6 hours
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall support reporting cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of their being noticed, with a copy to the sector regulator.

risk_register.title: Cyber security incidents reported promptly to RBI
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Cyber Security Framework in Banks §15 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall detect and log cyber security incidents and support reporting them to RBI (and CERT-In) within the mandated timelines.

risk_register.title: ICT system logs kept for a rolling 180 days within India
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(iv) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall keep logs of all its ICT components securely for a rolling 180 days, within India, and make them available to CERT-In on request.

risk_register.title: Suspicious and large cash transactions recorded and reported (STR/CTR)
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 §3 (G.S.R. 444(E)) [consolidated text, as amended])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall flag suspicious transactions and cash transactions above the prescribed threshold, keep their records, and produce suspicious- and cash-transaction reports for the Financial Intelligence Unit.

risk_register.title: System clocks synchronised to NIC/NPL time servers
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(i) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall synchronise all its clocks to the NIC or NPL NTP servers (or servers traceable to them), so that log timestamps are reliable.

risk_register.title: Transaction records kept at least five years from the date of transaction
risk_register.cause: REQ-011 covers this but states no period; at least 5 years is required. (Master Direction — Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016 §(a) (RBI/DBR/2015-16/18) [updated 14 Aug 2025])
risk_register.consequence: The obligation is only partly met, which an inspection will treat as unmet.
risk_register.mitigation: Strengthen the requirement: REQ-011 covers this but states no period; at least 5 years is required

risk_register.title: Infeasibility in REQ-006
risk_register.cause: The requirement assumes the system can distinguish between 'legacy COBOL service' and 'new Java service' active states for 'each transaction type' during a migration where features are being replicated. If REQ-001 is met (identical results), the services are functionally identical, making the distinction of 'which one is active' potentially logically inconsistent unless referring to infrastructure routing which is not defined.
risk_register.consequence: The requirement cannot be built or tested as written.
risk_register.mitigation: Clarify if this refers to a specific routing flag or if the UI should simply indicate 'System Under Maintenance' vs 'Normal Operation'. The current phrasing implies a capability that contradicts the goal of functional parity.

risk_register.title: Small team — key-person dependency
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "The project team consists of 2 developers and needs to be completed within 3-4 months."
risk_register.consequence: Losing one person stalls the project.
risk_register.mitigation: Pair on critical components, document as you go, and identify a backup for each area.
evidence: The project team consists of 2 developers and needs to be completed within 3-4 months.

risk_register.title: Integrations authenticated, encrypted and rate-limited
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (practice: Industry practice (OWASP API Security Top 10)).
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: Every integration with an external system shall be mutually authenticated, encrypted in transit, allow-listed and rate-limited, with failures logged.

risk_register.title: Sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §8.1 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall encrypt customer and transaction data at rest and in transit using algorithms and key lengths approved under the bank's cryptographic policy.

risk_register.title: High-risk function depends on an external system (REQ-002)
risk_register.cause: REQ-002 is high risk and classified Integration: The system shall execute automated regression tests at every stage of the migration process to verify that no existing functionality is broken.
risk_register.consequence: An external system's availability, contract or interface change blocks a high-risk function.
risk_register.mitigation: Agree interface contracts early, stub the dependency for testing, and define fallback behaviour.

risk_register.title: Legacy migration — undocumented behaviour and data conversion
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "A mid-sized private bank currently runs its core banking system on a legacy COBOL framework."
risk_register.consequence: Behaviour the old system relied on is lost or data is converted wrongly.
risk_register.mitigation: Inventory existing behaviour, reconcile migrated data, and run old and new in parallel before cut-over.
evidence: A mid-sized private bank currently runs its core banking system on a legacy COBOL framework.

risk_register.title: Insufficient team size for complex legacy-to-modern migration
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "The project team consists of 2 developers"
risk_register.consequence: Two developers are likely insufficient to handle the complexity of migrating a COBOL system to Java while maintaining exact feature replication and rigorous testing within the short timeline.
evidence: The project team consists of 2 developers

risk_register.title: Unrealistic timeline for full migration with zero new functionality
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "needs to be completed within 3-4 months"
risk_register.consequence: Completing a full system migration from COBOL to Java, including extensive testing and validation at every stage, in only 3-4 months is highly improbable given the technical debt and complexity involved.
evidence: needs to be completed within 3-4 months

risk_register.title: Input validated and secure coding practices applied
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (practice: OWASP ASVS (industry practice; not in the knowledge base)).
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall validate all input on the server side and be built and tested against the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard.

risk_register.title: Security events monitored and alerted on
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §19.6(b) (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall forward security events to the bank's security operations monitoring and raise alerts on anomalous access or activity.

risk_register.title: Vulnerability management, patching and security testing before release
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §7.1 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall undergo vulnerability assessment and penetration testing before go-live and after major changes, and its components shall be patched under the bank's patch management policy.

questions.question: Integrations authenticated, encrypted and rate-limited. Should the system include: “Every integration with an external system shall be mutually authenticated, encrypted in transit, allow-listed and rate-limited, with failures logged”?

Sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit. Should the system include: “The system shall encrypt customer and transaction data at rest and in transit using algorithms and key lengths approved under the bank's cryptographic policy”?

About “The system shall allow administrators to configure specific thresholds for data volume and transaction speed that trigger an alert when the…”: The stakeholder field is empty ('Not specified'). (For example: Identify the specific stakeholder (e.g., 'Performance Engineer' or 'SRE').)

About “The system shall archive all raw transaction logs and transformation records from the legacy COBOL system in a read-only format immediately…”: The term 'immediately' is not measurable; it does not specify a latency threshold (e.g., within 5 minutes, within 1 hour). (For example: Replace 'immediately' with a specific time-bound metric (e.g., 'within 5 minutes of successful processing').)

About “The system shall automatically retry failed data synchronization jobs between the legacy and new systems up to three times before escalatin…”: The stakeholder field is empty ('Not specified'). (For example: Identify the specific stakeholder (e.g., 'DevOps Lead' or 'Data Engineer').)

About “The system shall generate a daily reconciliation report comparing transaction counts and balances between the legacy COBOL system and the n…”: The term 'daily' is vague regarding the exact execution time window (e.g., 00:00 UTC, end of business day) and the definition of 'previous 24 hours' for batch processing. (For example: Specify the exact timestamp or cron schedule (e.g., 'at 01:00 UTC daily') and define the precise start/end boundaries for the 'previous 24 hours' calculation.)

About “The system shall provide a 'dry-run' mode that simulates data migration and transformation logic without actually writing to the production…”: The term 'dry-run' mode is used without a concrete definition of what constitutes a successful simulation versus a failure, making the acceptance criteria vague. (For example: Define specific exit codes or log markers that indicate a successful dry-run simulation versus an error state.)
